verdict.summary: Smartsheet lists the API as requiring a Business, Enterprise or Advanced Work Management plan, and app registration only opens after Smartsheet approves a Developer Tools request for your account. Once you're in, there's no app review: any Smartsheet user who consents can connect, though it's unclear whether customers on Pro plans can use API apps at all.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The build itself takes about an hour. The unknown is how long Smartsheet takes to accept the Developer Tools registration; no turnaround is published.

timeToProd.assumes: A Business-plan developer account with Developer Tools approved, and an app reading and writing sheets for customers on Business or higher plans.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Smartsheet accepting the Developer Tools registration. There is no app review after that.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The OAuth guide describes no review or approval for apps. The Developer Tools approval time is not documented.

verdict.cost: A Smartsheet Business, Enterprise or Advanced Work Management plan for the developer account (paid, per seat)

prerequisites.item: A Smartsheet account on a Business, Enterprise or Advanced Work Management plan
prerequisites.why: The API introduction lists these plans as required. Pro is not included.

prerequisites.item: A dedicated service account for owning the app (recommended)
prerequisites.why: Smartsheet says 'A best practice is to use an additional Smartsheet account' that you don't personally use.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Whether that extra account takes a paid seat is not stated in the OAuth guide.

prerequisites.item: Developer Tools activated, plus a developer profile
prerequisites.why: You register through the Developer Tools Registration page; 'Upon accepting your request, Smartsheet activates the Developer Tools user interface.' A developer profile is a prerequisite for registering apps.

prerequisites.item: An HTTPS redirect URL, app URL and support contact
prerequisites.why: App registration asks for a name, description, app URL, support contact and redirect URL, and the OAuth flow requires HTTPS.

scopeTiers.impact: Enough for an agent that reads sheets, reports and dashboards. Scopes never override the user's own sharing permissions.
Lets the agent update rows and create, share or delete sheets. Same self-serve consent; only request what you need.
Needed for webhooks and workspace/user administration. They only do anything when the consenting user already has those rights.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: 'Only work for admins' is our reading of 'scopes don't override sharing permissions'.

steps.title: Get a Business-plan account for the app
steps.detail: Set up (or designate) a Smartsheet service account on a Business, Enterprise or Advanced Work Management plan.

steps.title: Request Developer Tools
steps.detail: Open the Developer Tools Registration page from the OAuth guide and click Register User Account.

steps.title: Wait for Smartsheet to approve the request
steps.detail: Smartsheet activates the Developer Tools UI once it accepts the request. If it's denied, Smartsheet says to consult your Customer Success Manager.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: No turnaround time is published; the duration is our estimate.

steps.title: Create a developer profile and app
steps.detail: In Developer Tools, create the developer profile, then the app: name, description, app URL, support contact, HTTPS redirect URL and logo. Leave 'Publish App?' off unless you want a public profile page. Copy the client ID and secret.

steps.title: Implement the authorization code flow
steps.detail: Redirect to https://app.smartsheet.com/b/authorize with client_id, response_type=code, space-delimited scope and state. Exchange the code (valid about 10 minutes) at https://api.smartsheet.com/2.0/token with grant_type=authorization_code, sending either the secret or the documented hash parameter.

steps.title: Add refresh and retry handling
steps.detail: Refresh before the 7-day access token expires and store the new refresh token. On HTTP 429 with errorCode 4003, sleep 60 seconds and retry.

steps.title: Decide on regional support
steps.detail: Smartsheet Gov, Regions Europe and Regions Australia each have their own API host. Plan per-region base URLs and confirm whether each region needs its own app.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Whether apps and tokens are per region isn't stated on that page.

steps.title: Test with a second Smartsheet user
steps.detail: Authorize from another account, ideally one on the plan your customers use, and confirm reads and writes work.

steps.title: Launch
steps.detail: Ship the Connect Smartsheet button. No app review is documented.

agentCanDo: Implement the code flow, token exchange and refresh
Build retry on errorCode 4003 with a 60-second sleep
Map regional base URLs (Gov, EU, AU)
Draft the app description and support page
humanMustDo: Buy or designate a Business-plan service account
Request Developer Tools and follow up if denied
Create the developer profile and app and copy the secret
Test authorization with a second account

blockers.symptom: Developer Tools request denied, or the Developer Tools UI never appears
blockers.cause: Smartsheet hasn't accepted the registration, possibly because the account isn't on an eligible plan.
blockers.fix: Upgrade the account to Business or higher and contact your Customer Success Manager.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The link between plan and denial is our inference.

blockers.cause: Wrong client_id, or an app registered in a different Smartsheet region.
blockers.fix: Re-copy the client ID, and use the token host for the same region as the app.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Observed by POSTing dummy credentials to https://api.smartsheet.com/2.0/token on 2026-10-20. The region part is inferred.

blockers.cause: More than 300 requests per minute on one access token. File attachments and cell history count as 10 requests each.
blockers.fix: Sleep 60 seconds and retry, and spread work across connections.

blockers.symptom: API returns {"errorCode":1004,"message":"You are not authorized to perform this action."}
blockers.cause: Missing or invalid token, or the user lacks sharing rights on the object.
blockers.fix: Check the Authorization header and scopes, and remember scopes don't override sharing permissions.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Observed on GET https://api.smartsheet.com/2.0/users/me without a token on 2026-10-20.

blockers.symptom: Some customers can't use the integration
blockers.cause: The API is listed as Business, Enterprise or Advanced Work Management only, so Pro-plan customers may be blocked.
blockers.fix: State the plan requirement on your Connect page and test with a Pro account.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: Official docs state the plan requirement, but not clearly whether it applies to end users of third-party OAuth apps.

nuances.text: Access tokens expire after 604,799 seconds (about 7 days). A refresh returns a new access and refresh token pair. The refresh token's lifetime isn't documented.
Rate limit is 300 requests per minute per access token, and parallel workers sharing one token share that budget.
Smartsheet Gov (api.smartsheetgov.com), Regions Europe (api.smartsheet.eu) and Regions Australia (api.smartsheet.au) are separate hosts. A community thread says EU apps need an EU developer setup.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Hosts are official. The EU app requirement is from an undated community post.

nuances.text: 'Publish App?' only makes your app's profile page public. It is not a marketplace listing or a review gate.
The token exchange can send a hash of the code and secret instead of the raw client secret.
